statement.p: Compute the derivative of the given function in two different ways.
a) Use the Product Rule, [fg]' = f\cdot g' + f' \cdot g. (Fill in each blank, then simplify.)
b) Use algebra first to simplify h, then differentiate without the Product Rule.

static.solution:
Solution:
First, using the Product Rule,
\begin{array}{rcl} h'(s) \amp =\amp (9 s - 4) \cdot \frac{d}{dx}[ -8 s - 8 ] + \frac{d}{dx}[ 9 s - 4 ] (-8 s - 8)\\ \amp \amp \\ \amp =\amp (9 s - 4)(-8) + (9)(-8 s - 8) \\ \end{array} After simplifying the last line, we find h'(s) = -144 s - 40.
Next, simplify h first. Then take the derivative. \begin{array}{rcl} h(s) \amp =\amp (9 s - 4)(-8 s - 8) = -72 s^2 - 40 s + 32 \\ \amp \amp \\ h'(s) \amp =\amp -144 s - 40 \end{array} The two simplified answers should match.
